original_target.title: Decomposing complete graphs into squares of Hamilton cycles

full_original_statement:
For $`n\ge5`$, the square $`C_n^2`$ of an $`n`$-cycle joins every pair of vertices at cyclic distance one or two.

Prove or disprove that, whenever $`n\equiv1\pmod4`$ and $`n\ne9`$, the edges of the complete graph $`K_n`$ can be partitioned into copies of $`C_n^2`$. Thus the required decomposition consists of $`(n-1)/4`$ edge-disjoint spanning cycle squares.

sources.scope_comparison: The exact n=1 mod 4, n!=9 Hamilton-cycle-square decomposition is retained as Conjecture 4.1. Constructions for infinitely many primes and listed composite orders do not cover every admissible n. Simplicial diameter and extra-tight-tour solutions do not imply such edge decompositions.
